_why_no_mutations: Every other file in this directory is a set of mutations against product
source. This one cannot be, and the difference is the point.
ADR 0069's table is not a claim about the product's tests. It is a claim
about the HARNESS -- that a patch which does not apply, a replacement
identical to the original, and a suite that reports no test count are each
reported INDETERMINATE rather than 'not caught'. Those three are the three
ways the hand-run harness produced a wrong answer, and the fifth row (a
real mutation against a passing suite must read NOT CAUGHT) is what keeps
the other four from being satisfied by a harness that returns INDETERMINATE
There is no set of mutations that reproduces that. `mutate.py --selftest`
reproduces it exactly, and verify_build.py runs it on every build -- which
is a stronger guarantee than a set file, because a set file is re-runnable
_verified: 2026-08-16: run, and its five lines compared against the ADR's five rows
[ok] replacement identical to the original: INDETERMINATE
[ok] suite reports no test count: INDETERMINATE
[ok] a real mutation against a passing suite: NOT CAUGHT
_this_field_is_checked: command verify_build.py actually runs, and its --selftest drives the
refusal: a set file naming an unwired script, or a wired script with an
argument the build never passes, both fail.
Without that, `reproduced_by` would be a way out of the guard rather than a
second way of satisfying it -- any future record could opt out by naming a
command, and the guard would be back to trusting a label.
